definitions.definition: On ℝ^n and ℝ^m use the standard Euclidean inner product v·w=∑_k v_k w_k and norm |v|=(v·v)^(1/2). Spatial Lebesgue measure dx is the product of the n ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measures in the standard coordinates. For any function on ℝ^n×(0,∞), ∂_{x_j} means its componentwise derivative in spatial coordinate j (1≤j≤n), and ∂_t its componentwise time derivative, where these derivatives exist. In particular u_t=∂_t u, u_tt=∂_t(∂_t u), and ∂_{x_jx_j}u=∂_{x_j}(∂_{x_j}u). For scalar functions the same conventions apply. D_xu denotes the matrix with columns ∂_{x_j}u, and its squared Frobenius norm is ∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|². Smooth means derivatives of every finite order exist and are continuous on the stated open domain. An integral without a displayed measure is the Lebesgue integral; integrable means measurable with finite integral of the absolute value (or norm).

output.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is integrable. More precisely, for each t0>0 there exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n, R>0 and B≥0 such that, writing J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and Q=[−R,R]^n, one has C⊂(−R,R)^n, u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J, and all positive-order derivatives of u vanish for x∉C and r∈int J. The box Q has Lebesgue measure (2R)^n<∞. For every r∈int J, each of the spatial functions e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), evaluated at time r, is continuous, vanishes outside C, and is integrable on ℝ^n, for each 1≤j≤n. Finally |e_t(x,r)|≤B for all (x,r)∈Q×[3t0/4,5t0/4].

locals.declaration: Choose the compact C asserted by F001.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Both endpoints are positive and the left is strictly smaller than the right. H006 therefore supplies a compact spatial set on which the perturbation may be supported throughout J.

produces.statement: There exists a compact C⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈J.

argument.text: Choose C as in F001. Apply M006 with real codomain to the continuous Euclidean norm on C. It gives a real upper bound for |x| on C, including when C is empty.

produces.statement: There exists L∈ℝ such that |x|≤L for every x∈C.

argument.text: Choose L from F002 and set R=max(1,L+1), Q=[−R,R]^n. Then R>0 and for x∈C every coordinate satisfies |x_j|≤|x|≤L<R. Thus C⊂(−R,R)^n=int Q. H001 ensures the stated positive finite dimensions; Q is a compact product of closed bounded intervals. For the coordinate product Lebesgue measure its measure is the finite product ∏_{j=1}^n(2R)=(2R)^n<∞.

produces.statement: R>0, C⊂int Q=(−R,R)^n, Q is compact and its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞; u=q outside C throughout J.

argument.text: The set (ℝ^n\C)×int J is open, since compact C is closed in Euclidean space. There u is identically the fixed q by F001. At every point of this open set all positive-order coordinate derivatives vanish: the first derivative is the limit of zero difference quotients in a neighborhood, and repetition proves the assertion at every finite order. H002 gives continuity of all derivatives everywhere on the time-domain. Therefore, at any r∈int J, every spatial function in the output's list is continuous and zero off C; its nonzero set has closure contained in the closed compact C. Apply M005 to each of these functions. This proves all their integrability claims, including e(·,t0), e_t and every product used later. Equivalently, each is bounded in absolute value on Q by M006 and has absolute integral at most that bound times (2R)^n.

produces.statement: All positive-order derivatives of u vanish on (ℝ^n\C)×int J. At every r∈int J the spatial sections of e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u) are continuous, supported in C and integrable, for each 1≤j≤n.

argument.text: The closed time interval [3t0/4,5t0/4] lies in int J. The product Q×[3t0/4,5t0/4] is compact. H002 implies that e_t is continuous there, since e is a finite sum of squares of smooth component derivatives. Apply M006 to |e_t| on this space-time compact box to obtain a finite real upper bound.

produces.statement: There exists B0∈ℝ with |e_t(x,r)|≤B0 for all (x,r)∈Q×[3t0/4,5t0/4].

argument.text: Choose B0 as in F005 and put B=max(0,B0). Then B≥0 and the same bound holds with B. F003 and F004 give all the claimed support, measure and integrability assertions. In particular t0∈int J. Since t0 was arbitrary, e(·,t) is integrable at every positive time; the witnesses C,R,B establish the full more precise assertion.
